title: Colon adenocarcinoma
subtitle: 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90%, II 70–85%, III 50–73%, IV 12–14%
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Colon Cancer (Johnson T, Miller D) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Workup
items: MMR / MSI testing in ALL newly diagnosed colon cancer
KRAS, NRAS, BRAF mutation + HER2 amplification by NGS panel
CT C/A/P · MRI liver if potentially resectable liver mets · PET/CT in selected resectable M1
Genetics referral: all diagnosed <50 y, or somatic finding with germline implications
BRAF V600E + MLH1 loss largely excludes Lynch — but ~1% of Lynch is BRAF V600E

blocks.heading: Staging — AJCC 8th
rows: submucosa / through muscularis propria / into pericolorectal tissue
through visceral peritoneum / invades adjacent organ

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: 3 vs 6 mo adjuvant — failed non-inferiority overall (HR 1.07, margin 1.12), but 3 mo CAPOX non-inferior while FOLFOX favored 6 mo (Grothey, NEJM 2018)
adding IO to adjuvant chemo in dMMR (ASCO 2025)
1L pembrolizumab in dMMR: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 mo

boxes: no adjuvant therapy for stage I
risk factors: T4, LVI, PNI, obstruction,
IDEA: 3 mo CAPOX ok — FOLFOX needs 6 mo
high risk (T4 and/or N2) favors 6 months
FOLFOX or CAPEOX preferred — cure possible
swap backbone; HER2 matters in 2nd line

blocks.html: Oxaliplatin neuropathy is the dominant long-term toxicity. Six months may raise the risk of permanent neuropathy as much as tenfold vs three months. Do not exceed ~4 months in initial metastatic therapy (OPTIMOX); never given as a single agent.

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
rows: cetuximab 400 load then 250 weekly (or 500 q2wk) · panitumumab 6 mg/kg
ramp 80→120→160 mg weekly in C1; then 160 mg d1–21
35 mg/m² PO BID d1–5 and d8–12
blocks.footnote: All doses mg/m² unless stated. Institutional preference: no 5-FU bolus (higher toxicity) — which also removes the need for leucovorin as a stabilizer.

blocks.heading: Biomarker → therapy
rows: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk — 1L metastatic; also neoadjuvant/adjuvant
Cetuximab or panitumumab — no benefit if right-sided or RAS-mutant
Larotrectinib 100 mg BID · entrectinib 600 mg daily

blocks.heading: Surveillance
items: H&P + CEA q3–6 mo × 2 yr, then q6 mo — 5 years total
CT C/A/P: stage II–III q6–12 mo × 5 yr; stage IV q3–6 mo × 2 yr then q6–12 mo
Colonoscopy at 1 year post-op; within 3–6 mo if no complete pre-op scope
If adenoma found repeat in 1 yr; otherwise 3 yr, then every 5 yr

blocks.heading: Pearls & cautions
items: Irinotecan with great caution in the elderly, biliary obstruction, or hyperbilirubinemia
Regorafenib is very toxic — many do better at lower doses; bevacizumab benefit is modest
ctDNA timing conflict: results take 4–6 wk but adjuvant works best within 6 wk of surgery
Metastatic rectal regimens are identical to metastatic CRC

text: Colon adenocarcinoma 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90% , II 70–85% , III 50–73% , IV 12–14% Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Colon Cancer (Johnson T, Miller D) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Colonoscopy with biopsy + pathology review MMR / MSI testing in ALL newly diagnosed colon cancer KRAS, NRAS, BRAF mutation + HER2 amplification by NGS panel CT C/A/P · MRI liver if potentially resectable liver mets · PET/CT in selected resectable M1 Labs: CBC, CMP, CEA Genetics referral: all diagnosed <50 y , or somatic finding with germline implications BRAF V600E + MLH1 loss largely excludes Lynch — but ~1% of Lynch is BRAF V600E Staging — AJCC 8th T1 / T2 / T3 submucosa / through muscularis propria / into pericolorectal tissue T4a / T4b through visceral peritoneum / invades adjacent organ N1 / N2 1–3 nodes (N1c = deposits only) / ≥4 nodes M1a / b / c 1 site / ≥2 sites / peritoneal Stage III any node-positive, M0 Key trials IDEA 3 vs 6 mo adjuvant — failed non-inferiority overall (HR 1.07, margin 1.12), but 3 mo CAPOX non-inferior while FOLFOX favored 6 mo (Grothey, NEJM 2018) ATOMIC adding IO to adjuvant chemo in dMMR (ASCO 2025) KEYNOTE-177 1L pembrolizumab in dMMR: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 mo BREAKWATER 1L BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab BEACON BRAF V600E later line (Kopetz, NEJM 2019) Treatment pathway Localized — stage I to III Surgery first colon is resected upfront (unlike rectal) pathology drives the adjuvant decision no adjuvant therapy for stage I Stage II (node-negative) risk factors: T4, LVI, PNI, obstruction, perforation, poor differentiation, <12 nodes low risk observe; RFs 5-FU ± oxaliplatin Stage III virtually all receive adjuvant chemotherapy age <75: fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin age >75: fluoropyrimidine alone IDEA: 3 mo CAPOX ok — FOLFOX needs 6 mo high risk (T4 and/or N2) favors 6 months dMMR / MSI-H Immunotherapy-sensitive consider neoadjuvant IO before resection adjuvant: add IO to chemo (ATOMIC) adjuvant 5-FU alone may be HARMFUL Metastatic Oligometastatic liver/lung only: surgical consult upfront FOLFOX or CAPEOX preferred — cure possible 1L by molecular subtype dMMR: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177) BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab left-sided RAS/BRAF WT: doublet + anti-EGFR right-sided or RAS-mut: FOLFOXIRI ± bev Later lines stop oxaliplatin at ~4 months (neuropathy) swap backbone; HER2 matters in 2nd line Oxaliplatin neuropathy is the dominant long-term toxicity. Six months may raise the risk of permanent neuropathy as much as tenfold vs three months. Do not exceed ~4 months in initial metastatic therapy (OPTIMOX); never given as a single agent. Institutional preference: no 5-FU bolus (higher toxicity) — which also removes the need for leucovorin as a stabilizer.
